method: All seven official/author URLs opened and relevant sections read through web retrieval. Library behavior separately executed at stated versions.

sources.title: NumPy 2.3 Broadcasting
sources.supports: Trailing dimensions align; equal or size-one axes broadcast. A (n,1) minus (n,) yields (n,n).
sources.verification_and_limits: Actual NumPy 2.3.5 residual shape and gradient checked in library_check.py.

sources.title: SciPy 1.17.0 check_grad
sources.supports: Uses forward differences, configurable epsilon, and returns a Euclidean norm of analytic-versus-approximate gradient difference.
sources.verification_and_limits: Explicit epsilon=1e-6, direction=all; quadratic forward error independently predicted from diagonal Hessian. Not confused with central differences.

sources.title: NumPy 2.3 finfo
sources.supports: eps is the spacing above one; smallest_normal differs from smallest_subnormal; finite dynamic range and reduced subnormal precision.
sources.verification_and_limits: Documentation read; numerical extreme-tail behavior independently checked with Decimal and actual libraries.

sources.title: NumPy 2.3 logaddexp
sources.verification_and_limits: Actual NumPy 2.3.5 logaddexp(0,t), binary64, finite t in [-2000,2000], compared to authored formula and Decimal.

sources.title: SciPy 1.17.0 logsumexp
sources.supports: axis selects reduction axes; axis=None reduces all; keepdims retains singleton reduced axes; weighted and signed cases have additional semantics.
sources.verification_and_limits: Actual SciPy 1.17.0 axis=1 and keepdims shapes checked, two-column softplus and three-term extreme rows. Weighted/nonfinite cases not claimed.

sources.title: SciPy 1.17.0 log_expit
sources.supports: Computes log sigmoid while avoiding precision loss from log(expit(x)) at large positive or negative values.
sources.verification_and_limits: Actual SciPy 1.17.0 -log_expit(-t) and expit(t) compared to stable losses and local derivatives on the same rows.

sources.title: Nicholas J. Higham, What Is the Log-Sum-Exp Function, 2021
sources.supports: Author discussion of log-sum-exp, numerical range and shifting by the maximum.
sources.verification_and_limits: Article read. The lesson derives the identity independently and tests its finite-input use; no third-party text or figure copied.

authorship: Data, derivations, figures, examples and wording are original. No third-party full text is bundled.
scope: No claim to test PyTorch, GPU, weighted BCE, soft-label BCE, nonfinite LSE, browser UI or Anaconda installation.
